title: Mud like saffron
told: a sakhi of Guru Nanak and Bhai Lehna, a traditional story

hook.say: before the story, a question. what’s a job you secretly think is beneath you?
options: honest. me too, some days. listen.
ha. you’ll like this one. listen.
then you’d have gotten along with lehna. listen.

steps.line: Remember Lehna, who found the Guru holding his reins? He stayed at Kartarpur, where Guru Nanak now farmed the land like everyone else.
steps.label: a traditional sakhi

steps.line: One rainy day, a heavy bundle of wet grass, dripping mud, had to be carried home for the cattle. The Guru asked his sons. They refused.

steps.q: Lehna lifts the dripping bundle, fine clothes and all, and carries it home. Who do you think is upset?
steps.why: Mata Sulakhni, Guru Nanak’s wife, worried for her guest’s clothes. Lehna was a trader’s son from Khadur who had come to Kartarpur and stayed to serve.

steps.line: Lehna lifted it onto his head, fine clothes and all, and carried it home. Mud ran down his clothes.
The Guru’s wife was upset: your guest’s clothes are ruined! The Guru smiled and said: that isn’t mud. It’s saffron.

steps.q: Why would the Guru call the mud saffron?
o: Mud from humble service is precious
The wet grass had stained the mud yellow
He was teasing his sons for refusing
steps.why: Saffron was costly, and its color, kesri, still flies on many Sikh flags. Mud from serving, the Guru said, was worth more.

steps.line: Later, the Guru chose who would follow him. Not his sons: Lehna. He placed five coins and a coconut before him, and bowed.
He gave him a new name, Angad, from ang, a limb: part of my own body. He became the second Guru.

steps.q: As the second Guru, Angad left a gift Sikhs still read every day. What?
steps.why: Tradition credits Guru Angad with shaping Gurmukhi, the script of the Guru Granth Sahib. The Golden Temple came with the fifth Guru, the Khalsa with the tenth.

steps.q: Guru Nanak set five coins and a coconut before Lehna, and bowed. Why does the bow matter?
o: It was how guests were greeted in Punjab
He was thanking Lehna for the grass
The teacher now bowed to the new Guru
steps.why: The same light passed from one Guru to the next, so the first Guru bowed to it. Tradition says later Gurus were installed the same way.

say: remember tera, yours? guru nanak didn’t hold on to anything as his own, not even the guruship. he gave it away, past his own sons, to the one with open hands.
and lehna held nothing as his either, not even his clean clothes. sikhs call the sense of “me and mine” haumai, ego, the wall between us and god. tera takes the wall down, one bundle at a time.

steps.q: From the story, why did Guru Nanak pass over his own sons?
o: They were too young to lead
They lived too far from Kartarpur
It went to service, not to blood
steps.why: Not by blood. By open hands. Guru Nanak chose his disciple over both his sons.

today.say: today, pick one job you think is beneath you, the dishes, the trash, the mess someone else left, and do it quietly, without being asked. say tera under your breath if you like.
options: then wear the mud like saffron.
